Concrete scenario: Swarm of Ravens Beaks (PDF p.391) prints reach 5 ft., "one target in the swarm’s space", but emits target "one target". A target five feet away outside the swarm's space satisfies the projected range/target while violating the source restriction. Giant Crocodile Tail similarly loses "not grappled by the crocodile"; Vampire/Vampire Spawn Bite loses the alternative eligible grappled/incapacitated/restrained targets. Retained raw text does not satisfy the explicit complete-target projection criterion.
Sibling analysis: Searched all creature narrative attack groups, including the actual legendaryActions.entries shape. Nine affected attacks: giant-crocodile Tail; swarm-of-bats/insects/poisonous-snakes/quippers/rats Bites; swarm-of-ravens Beaks; vampire Bite (Bat or Vampire Form Only); vampire-spawn Bite. Verified the qualifiers directly in the PDF (crocodile pp.374-375, swarms pp.389-391, vampire pp.353-354, spawn p.354). Both exclusion/space restrictions and alternative eligible targets are affected by the same early regex termination. Qualifiers before the creature/target noun, such as size restrictions, already survive; qualifiers after it do not.
Required closure: Preserve the entire source target phrase through the pre-Hit sentence boundary for this grammar, regenerate every affected sibling, and add proportionate permanent evidence: a generalized source-target fidelity invariant plus a representative exact vendored-source case. This directly protects the named defect class without requiring an engine implementation. S2 — BLOCKING: Top-level damage for an alternative attack violates the authorized default-mode-only contract.

Its acceptance criteria also require source relationships to survive projection. Location: packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/mechanicsProjections.ts:669; packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json:58172.
Concrete scenario: Swarm of Poisonous Snakes Bites (PDF p.390) has default hitDamage [7 (2d6) piercing] and half-HP alternative [3 (1d6) piercing]. The poison is separately governed by DC 10 Constitution, 14 (4d6) on failure and half on success. The new projector appends that separate sentence's poison term to mechanics.damage, yielding [2d6 piercing, 4d6 poison], rather than the promised default hit-mode list. A consumer using that designated default summary receives save-governed damage without its relationship to the save. This is an actual representation-contract mismatch; no current deterministic damage execution is asserted.
Sibling analysis: Checked every alternative-bearing attack (27 entries, 28 alternative modes). Poisonous Snakes is the sole current entry where separately printed damage outside the Hit sentence makes mechanics.damage differ from the default hitDamage. Azer, Erinyes, and Salamander have genuine shared plus-riders inside the Hit clause and correctly retain those riders in every complete mode. Checked both full-HP/half-HP mode selection and failed/successful-save dimensions; the mode and save are independent.
Required closure: Make the alternative-bearing entry's mechanics.damage follow the authorized default-mode-only contract, while retaining the separately printed save clause and its damage faithfully for adjudication. Do not erase the poison source or confuse it with a shared unconditional Hit rider. Add proportionate permanent evidence: an exact source-backed Poisonous Snakes assertion of the default/top-level relationship and preservation of the separate save clause, retaining the existing shared-rider protections. Repair is MATERIAL (projection contract/generated data); fresh full review of the repaired head is required.
